# Test Beta Correlations as Approximations of Variant Correlations

The idea here is to provide some empirical evidence that correlations between 
the betas in a GWAS might be good estimates of the correlations between the 
variants themselves. To that end, I am simulating two variants with some degree
of correlation between them and different types of traits to predict from the 
variants. 

In all experiments the variants are being simulated in the following way:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Simulate variant A using allele frequencies and assumption of HWE.
\item Simulate variant B by picking the variant A genotype with some probability.
\item Otherwise pick the variant B genotype at random.
\end{enumerate}

As a result of this simulation approach variant B might not always be in HWE, 
but it should be close enough, that it shouldn't matter. 

### 1) Load in Libraries and Set global Variables

```{r} 
#Call needed libraries
library(faux)
library(tidyverse)
library(pbapply)
library(matlib)

#Set allele frequency for variant a and correlation for variant b
aaf_a = 0.2
prob_same <- 0.6 #Probability of variants having same genotype
#Set number of people and traits
pop=100000
traits=500
```

### 2) Test Beta Correlation Approximation for Randomized Traits

For this test, the traits are generated completely at random selecting each 
person's trait value using a uniform distribution from 0 to 1. This simulation
is similar to the case where we're looking at non-genetic traits or loci that 
are unassociated to the traits. 

```{r}
#Create a function to calculate correlations of variants and betas
test_correlations_random_traits <- function(test_combo, n=pop, m=traits){
  #Extract values from test combo
  aaf_a <- test_combo[1]
  prob_same <- test_combo[2]
  
  #Simulate a variant
  variant_a = sample(0:2, n, replace = TRUE, prob = c((1-aaf_a)^2, (1-aaf_a)*aaf_a, aaf_a^2))
  # Generate b variant with desired correlation
  variant_b <- vector()
  get_variant_b <- function(a_value, corr_ab=prob_same){return(ifelse(runif(1)< corr_ab, a_value, sample(0:2, 1, replace=TRUE)))}
  variant_b <- vapply(variant_a, get_variant_b, FUN.VALUE = numeric(1))
  #Combine into variant matrix 
  variant_matrix <- cbind.data.frame(variant_a, variant_b)
  
  # Create a matrix of random values
  random_traits <- matrix(runif(n * m), nrow = n, ncol = m)
  # Center the data
  variant_matrix_centered <- scale(variant_matrix, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
  random_traits_centered <- scale(random_traits, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)

  # Compute covariance between predictors and traits
  cov_xy <- t(variant_matrix_centered) %*% random_traits_centered  # (m_predictors x t_traits)
  # Compute variance of each predictor
  var_x <- colSums(variant_matrix_centered^2)  # (m_predictors)
  # Calculate betas
  trait_betas <- cov_xy / var_x  # (m_predictors x t_traits)
  
  #Calculate correlations between betas and variants
  cor_betas <- cor(trait_betas[1,], trait_betas[2,])
  cor_vars <- cor(variant_a, variant_b)
  #Calculate difference between values
  diff_cor = cor_vars - cor_betas
  #Return desired values 
  return(c(cor_vars, cor_betas, diff_cor))
}

#Create a range of aafs and sameness probabilities to test over
aafs <- seq(0.01,0.49,0.1)
same_probs <- seq(0.1,1,0.05)
testing_combos <- as.matrix(expand.grid(aafs, same_probs))

#Run test
random_results <- pbapply(testing_combos, MARGIN = 1, FUN = test_correlations_random_traits)
rownames(random_results) <- c("cor_vars", "cor_betas", "diff_cor")
random_results <- t(random_results)

#Plot correlations
ggplot(random_results, mapping = aes(cor_vars, cor_betas)) + geom_point() + 
  xlab("Variant Correlation") + ylab("Beta Correlation") + ggtitle("Null Effects Test") + 
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color="darkgrey") + 
    theme(panel.background = element_blank(), legend.title = element_blank(), axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
          axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, angle=45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1), plot.title = element_text(size=20, color="black", hjust=0.5),
          legend.position = "none", axis.text.y = element_text(size=12), axis.title = element_text(size = 16))
```

### 2) Test joint causal effects of SNPs 

In this test, we assume that both variants have an effect on one phenotype each. 
For their respective traits, each variant adds a value to the trait equal to 
their effect size times the number of alternate allele copies. 

```{r}
#Create a function to calculate correlations of variants and betas
test_correlations_causal_effects <- function(test_combo, n=pop, m=traits){
  #Extract values from test combo
  aaf_a <- test_combo[1]
  prob_same <- test_combo[2]
  effect_size <- test_combo[3]
  
  #Simulate a variant
  variant_a = sample(0:2, n, replace = TRUE, prob = c((1-aaf_a)^2, (1-aaf_a)*aaf_a, aaf_a^2))
  # Generate b variant with desired correlation
  variant_b <- vector()
  get_variant_b <- function(a_value, corr_ab=prob_same){return(ifelse(runif(1)< corr_ab, a_value, sample(0:2, 1, replace=TRUE)))}
  variant_b <- vapply(variant_a, get_variant_b, FUN.VALUE = numeric(1))
  #Combine into variant matrix 
  variant_matrix <- cbind.data.frame(variant_a, variant_b)
  
  #Simulate phenotypes 
  # Create a matrix of random values
  random_traits <- matrix(runif(n * m), nrow = n, ncol = m)
  #Overwrite first trait to have causal effect from A
  random_traits[,1] <- random_traits[,1] + (effect_size * variant_a)
  #Overwrite first trait to have causal effect from B
  random_traits[,2] <- random_traits[,2] + (effect_size * variant_b)
  # Center the data
  variant_matrix_centered <- scale(variant_matrix, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
  random_traits_centered <- scale(random_traits, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
  
  # Compute covariance between predictors and traits
  cov_xy <- t(variant_matrix_centered) %*% random_traits_centered  # (m_predictors x t_traits)
  # Compute variance of each predictor
  var_x <- colSums(variant_matrix_centered^2)  # (m_predictors)
  # Calculate betas
  trait_betas <- cov_xy / var_x  # (m_predictors x t_traits)
  
  #Calculate correlations between betas and variants
  cor_betas <- cor(trait_betas[1,], trait_betas[2,])
  cor_vars <- cor(variant_a, variant_b)
  #Calculate difference between values
  diff_cor = cor_vars - cor_betas
  #Return desired values 
  return(c(cor_vars, cor_betas, diff_cor))
}

#Create a range of aafs and sameness probabilities to test over
aafs <- seq(0.05,0.4,0.05)
same_probs <- seq(0.1,1,0.1)
effect_sizes <- seq(0.1,1,0.1)
testing_combos <- as.matrix(expand.grid(aafs, same_probs, effect_sizes))

#Run test
causal_results <- pbapply(testing_combos, MARGIN = 1, FUN = test_correlations_causal_effects)
rownames(causal_results) <- c("cor_vars", "cor_betas", "diff_cor")
causal_results <- t(causal_results)

#Plot correlations
ggplot(causal_results, mapping = aes(cor_vars, cor_betas)) + geom_point() + 
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color="darkgrey") + 
  xlab("Variant Correlation") + ylab("Beta Correlation") + ggtitle("Joint Causal Effects Test") + 
    theme(panel.background = element_blank(), legend.title = element_blank(), axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
          axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, angle=45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1), plot.title = element_text(size=20, color="black", hjust=0.5),
          legend.position = "none", axis.text.y = element_text(size=12), axis.title = element_text(size = 16))
```

### 3) Test Correlated Traits 

This test is similar to the first one in that the variants again do not affect 
the phenotype. However, now the traits themselves are strongly correlated. This 
effect is achieved by simulating a single trait and then adding random noise to
it. 

```{r}
#Create a function to calculate correlations of variants and betas
test_correlations_correlated_traits <- function(test_combo, n=pop, m=traits){
  #Extract values from test combo
  aaf_a <- test_combo[1]
  prob_same <- test_combo[2]
  
  #Simulate a variant
  variant_a = sample(0:2, n, replace = TRUE, prob = c((1-aaf_a)^2, (1-aaf_a)*aaf_a, aaf_a^2))
  # Generate b variant with desired correlation
  variant_b <- vector()
  get_variant_b <- function(a_value, corr_ab=prob_same){return(ifelse(runif(1)< corr_ab, a_value, sample(0:2, 1, replace=TRUE)))}
  variant_b <- vapply(variant_a, get_variant_b, FUN.VALUE = numeric(1))
  #Combine into variant matrix 
  variant_matrix <- cbind.data.frame(variant_a, variant_b)
  
  #Simulate phenotypes 
  # Create a matrix of random values
  temp = runif(n)
  random_traits <- matrix(rep(temp, m), nrow = n, ncol = m, byrow = FALSE) + matrix(runif(n * m, min = -0.01, max=0.01), nrow = n, ncol = m)
  # Center the data
  variant_matrix_centered <- scale(variant_matrix, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
  random_traits_centered <- scale(random_traits, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
  
  # Compute covariance between predictors and traits
  cov_xy <- t(variant_matrix_centered) %*% random_traits_centered  # (m_predictors x t_traits)
  # Compute variance of each predictor
  var_x <- colSums(variant_matrix_centered^2)  # (m_predictors)
  # Calculate betas
  trait_betas <- cov_xy / var_x  # (m_predictors x t_traits)
  
  #Calculate correlations between betas and variants
  cor_betas <- cor(trait_betas[1,], trait_betas[2,])
  cor_vars <- cor(variant_a, variant_b)
  #Calculate difference between values
  diff_cor = cor_vars - cor_betas
  #Return desired values 
  return(c(cor_vars, cor_betas, diff_cor))
}

#Create a range of aafs and sameness probabilities to test over
aafs <- seq(0.01,0.49,0.1)
same_probs <- seq(0.1,1,0.05)
testing_combos <- as.matrix(expand.grid(aafs, same_probs))

#Run test
correlated_traits_results <- apply(testing_combos, MARGIN = 1, FUN = test_correlations_correlated_traits)
rownames(correlated_traits_results) <- c("cor_vars", "cor_betas", "diff_cor")
correlated_traits_results <- t(correlated_traits_results)

#Plot correlations
ggplot(correlated_traits_results, mapping = aes(cor_vars, cor_betas)) + geom_point() + 
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color="darkgrey") + 
  xlab("Variant Correlation") + ylab("Beta Correlation") + ggtitle("Correlated Traits Test") + 
    theme(panel.background = element_blank(), legend.title = element_blank(), axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
          axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, angle=45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1), plot.title = element_text(size=20, color="black", hjust=0.5),
          legend.position = "none", axis.text.y = element_text(size=12), axis.title = element_text(size = 16))
```


### 4) Test joint causal effects of SNPs with trait normalization

For this test, the traits are again generated completely at random selecting 
each person's trait value using a uniform distribution from 0 to 1. This 
simulation is similar to the first case where we were looking at non-genetic 
traits or loci that are unassociated to the traits. However, now we are varying
the number of null traits. 

```{r}
#Create a function to calculate correlations of variants and betas
test_correlations_num_traits <- function(test_combo, n=pop){
  #Extract values from test combo
  aaf_a <- test_combo[1]
  prob_same <- test_combo[2]
  m <- test_combo[3]
  
  #Simulate a variant
  variant_a = sample(0:2, n, replace = TRUE, prob = c((1-aaf_a)^2, (1-aaf_a)*aaf_a, aaf_a^2))
  # Generate b variant with desired correlation
  variant_b <- vector()
  get_variant_b <- function(a_value, corr_ab=prob_same){return(ifelse(runif(1)< corr_ab, a_value, sample(0:2, 1, replace=TRUE)))}
  variant_b <- vapply(variant_a, get_variant_b, FUN.VALUE = numeric(1))
  #Combine into variant matrix 
  variant_matrix <- cbind.data.frame(variant_a, variant_b)
  
  #Simulate phenotypes 
  # Create a matrix of random values
  random_traits <- matrix(runif(n * m), nrow = n, ncol = m)
  # Center the data
  variant_matrix_centered <- scale(variant_matrix, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
  random_traits_centered <- scale(random_traits, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
  
  # Compute covariance between predictors and traits
  cov_xy <- t(variant_matrix_centered) %*% random_traits_centered  # (m_predictors x t_traits)
  # Compute variance of each predictor
  var_x <- colSums(variant_matrix_centered^2)  # (m_predictors)
  # Calculate betas
  trait_betas <- cov_xy / var_x  # (m_predictors x t_traits)
  
  #Calculate correlations between betas and variants
  cor_betas <- cor(trait_betas[1,], trait_betas[2,])
  cor_vars <- cor(variant_a, variant_b)
  #Calculate difference between values
  diff_cor = cor_vars - cor_betas
  #Return desired values 
  return(c(cor_vars, cor_betas, diff_cor, m))
}

#Create a range of aafs and sameness probabilities to test over
aafs <- seq(0.01,0.49,0.1)
same_probs <- seq(0.1,1,0.05)
num_traits <- c(10,50,100,500,1000)
testing_combos <- as.matrix(expand.grid(aafs, same_probs, num_traits))

#Run test
num_traits_results <- pbapply(testing_combos, MARGIN = 1, FUN = test_correlations_num_traits)
rownames(num_traits_results) <- c("cor_vars", "cor_betas", "diff_cor", "num_traits")
num_traits_results <- as.data.frame(t(num_traits_results))

#Plot correlations
ggplot(num_traits_results, mapping = aes(cor_vars, cor_betas, color=num_traits)) + geom_point() + 
  xlab("Variant Correlation") + ylab("Beta Correlation") + ggtitle("Number of Traits Test (n=100K)") + 
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color="darkgrey") + scale_colour_gradientn(colours=rainbow(5)) +
    theme(panel.background = element_blank(), legend.title = element_blank(), axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
          axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, angle=45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1), plot.title = element_text(size=20, color="black", hjust=0.5),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size=12), axis.title = element_text(size = 16))
```

### 5) Test Randomized Traits with Variable Sample Sizes

For this test, the traits are again generated completely at random selecting each 
person's trait value using a uniform distribution from 0 to 1. However, now the 
population sizes are varied in order to see how large the population has to be
in order for the estimates to stabilize.

```{r}
#Create a function to calculate correlations of variants and betas
test_correlations_pop_size <- function(test_combo, m=traits){
  #Extract values from test combo
  aaf_a <- test_combo[1]
  prob_same <- test_combo[2]
  n <- test_combo[3]
  
  #Simulate a variant
  variant_a = sample(0:2, n, replace = TRUE, prob = c((1-aaf_a)^2, (1-aaf_a)*aaf_a, aaf_a^2))
  # Generate b variant with desired correlation
  variant_b <- vector()
  get_variant_b <- function(a_value, corr_ab=prob_same){return(ifelse(runif(1)< corr_ab, a_value, sample(0:2, 1, replace=TRUE)))}
  variant_b <- vapply(variant_a, get_variant_b, FUN.VALUE = numeric(1))
  #Combine into variant matrix 
  variant_matrix <- cbind.data.frame(variant_a, variant_b)
  
  #Simulate phenotypes 
  # Create a matrix of random values
  random_traits <- matrix(runif(n * m), nrow = n, ncol = m)
  # Center the data
  variant_matrix_centered <- scale(variant_matrix, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
  random_traits_centered <- scale(random_traits, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
  
  # Compute covariance between predictors and traits
  cov_xy <- t(variant_matrix_centered) %*% random_traits_centered  # (m_predictors x t_traits)
  # Compute variance of each predictor
  var_x <- colSums(variant_matrix_centered^2)  # (m_predictors)
  # Calculate betas
  trait_betas <- cov_xy / var_x  # (m_predictors x t_traits)
  
  #Calculate correlations between betas and variants
  cor_betas <- cor(trait_betas[1,], trait_betas[2,])
  cor_vars <- cor(variant_a, variant_b)
  #Calculate difference between values
  diff_cor = cor_vars - cor_betas
  #Return desired values 
  return(c(cor_vars, cor_betas, diff_cor, n))
}

#Create a range of aafs and sameness probabilities to test over
aafs <- seq(0.01,0.46,0.1)
same_probs <- seq(0.1,1,0.1)
pop_sizes <- c(100, 500, 1000, 5000, 10000, 50000)
testing_combos <- as.matrix(expand.grid(aafs, same_probs, pop_sizes))

#Run test
pop_size_results <- pbapply(testing_combos, MARGIN = 1, FUN = test_correlations_pop_size)
rownames(pop_size_results) <- c("cor_vars", "cor_betas", "diff_cor", "pop_size")
pop_size_results <- t(pop_size_results)

#Plot correlations
ggplot(pop_size_results, mapping = aes(cor_vars, cor_betas, color=pop_size)) + geom_point() + 
  xlab("Variant Correlation") + ylab("Beta Correlation") + ggtitle("Population Size Test (m = 500)") + 
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color="darkgrey") + scale_colour_gradientn(colours=rainbow(5)) +
    theme(panel.background = element_blank(), legend.title = element_blank(), axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
          axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, angle=45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1), plot.title = element_text(size=20, color="black", hjust=0.5),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size=12), axis.title = element_text(size = 16))
```


### 6) Test Variable Sample Sizes with Fewer Traits 

This is the same test as the line above, but now I've shrunk the number of traits.

```{r}

#Create a range of aafs and sameness probabilities to test over
aafs <- seq(0.01,0.46,0.1)
same_probs <- seq(0,1,0.1)

          axis.text.y = element_text(size=12), axis.title = element_text(size = 16))
```
